svg.title: E3 authority synthetic directed graph
svg.desc: Offline edge view. Repeated boxes refer to the same logical node IDs. Synthetic architecture only, not service or recovery validation. Red dashed edges are rejected designs.

text.tspan: E3 directed authority — synthetic edge view
Arrow: from exercises the listed permission over to. Credential, delegation and revocation belong to that edge. Repeated node boxes are
occurrences of the same logical record node. No deployed authority was inspected.
E3-AE01
Issue only locally approved role assertions with issuer/audience/15-minute
expiry and local revocation checks.
E3-A-ID
Local identity authority
E3-A-OP
Local operator
Credential: Protected local signing credential and separately enrolled operator method; fixture uses an ephemeral in-memory HMAC key only.
Delegation: Local identity custodian enrolls/approves operators; no corporate automatic entitlement.
Revoke — Local identity custodian: Disable local identity and record local revocation; deny sessions at local enforcement.
Timing/residual: Proposed immediate local deny on next action; actual system timing untested. Fixture revocation is not real AD/PKI/token-service revocation.
E3-AE02
Request synthetic telemetry.read and alarm.ack only while all local
prerequisites remain valid.
E3-A-OP
Local operator
E3-A-POLICY
Locally approved policy
Credential: Local audience-bound unexpired credential plus local role and approved policy version.
Delegation: Local operations/safety owners define permitted functions.
Revoke — Local policy/identity owners: Remove role/action mapping, revoke identity/session and verify deny.
Timing/residual: Next modeled action; real enforcement untested. Previously observed information is not recalled; no physical action is granted.
E3-AE03
Authorize only hazard-approved mediated operations in a future real
implementation; all physical actuation is denied by this model.
E3-A-POLICY
Locally approved policy
E3-A-MED
Legacy-device mediation boundary
Credential: Local service identity with segment/protocol/action allow-list, not a cloud token dependency.
Delegation: Site safety and OT owners approve exact mediated commands.
Revoke — Local OT security and safety owners: Disable mediation route/action under hazard-approved response, retaining safety interlocks.
Timing/residual: Must be established by actual hazard-reviewed test. Legacy devices may have independent local access paths needing physical/segment controls.
E3-AE04
Append local authorization/security events; cannot silently overwrite retained
history.
E3-A-POLICY
Locally approved policy
E3-A-LOG
Local telemetry/evidence store
Credential: Local append-only service identity; fixture stores a hash-linked in-memory array.
Delegation: Local evidence owner defines retention, capacity and export policy.
Revoke — Local OT security lead: Remove producer permission and preserve existing evidence/integrity anchor.
Timing/residual: Local enforcement target; actual service untested. A hash chain without independent anchoring is not tamper-proof or durable.
E3-AE05
Manage local signing-key lifecycle under independent custody; no operator role
approval or safety override.
E3-A-KEY
Local key custodian
E3-A-ID
Local identity authority
Credential: Local protected key-admin method; no online vault retrieval dependency.
Delegation: Local key authority approves rotation/recovery with validity bounds.
Revoke — Independent local key authority: Remove key-admin access and rotate/reissue within approved safe recovery plan.
Timing/residual: Site-specific; untested. Offline trust/revocation distribution and old signatures require reconciliation.
E3-AE06
Stop/veto operation and approve only the safety half of restart; never
overridden by central cyber authority.
E3-A-SAFETY
Independent local safety
authority
E3-A-RESTART
Local restart approval gate
Credential: Locally controlled safety-role approval and independent physical interlock authority; fixture is only a role flag.
Delegation: Actual site safety governance/hazard analysis, absent from this synthetic example.
Revoke — Local safety governance authority: Replace/withdraw safety authorization through approved local process; default is no restart.
Timing/residual: No unsafe automatic timeout override. The model does not exercise a physical stop or safety-rated system.
E3-AE07
Approve recovery-readiness half only after local
identity/policy/key/time/DNS/PKI/evidence reconciliation.
E3-A-REC
Local recovery custodian
E3-A-RESTART
Local restart approval gate
Credential: Independent local recovery method and known-good offline baseline.
Delegation: Local recovery owner; requires separate safety approval.
Revoke — Local recovery governance authority: Remove recovery role/approval; safe-stop persists until both local roles are valid.
Timing/residual: Next modeled restart attempt; actual untested. A recovered service is not safe to run merely because cyber checks pass.
Forbidden authority paths:
Central observer/corporate IdP → local runtime or safety privilege
Local policy/deployment identity → safety restart approval
Local operator → physical actuation in the supplied model
Cloud vault/online CRL/central ITSM → mandatory local bootstrap
One custodian → key issuance, evidence erasure and unilateral safety restart
